record_identity.title: Border Patrol facial recognition identification reportedly preceded Global Entry revocation

incident_identity.historical_event_name: Border Patrol facial recognition identification reportedly preceded Global Entry revocation
incident_identity.date_basis: Cleland places the agent’s facial-recognition statement on January 10 and the revocation notice on January 13.

summary: Nicole Cleland says an agent at a Minneapolis ICE operation addressed her by name on 10 January and said agents had facial recognition and body-camera recording. She received notice three days later that Global Entry and TSA PreCheck privileges were revoked. She reported fear and paused observing ICE activity while continuing peaceful protests. The notice did not give a definite reason.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: Cleland’s sworn declaration records an agent’s facial-recognition statement, not a described observed scan, identified app or independently verified match. It separately records January 13 revocation and reported fear. The account does not establish that facial recognition caused revocation. Ars supplies no agency confirmation of system or decision chain.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The reported biometric-identification claim and later status revocation make identity and agency protection relevant. The assessment remains unresolved because system identity and the causal decision chain are unconfirmed. Temporal sequence is not treated as proof of causation. Harm Impact: The Harm Impact result is SU. Executed AI biometric identification and the decision chain materially connecting it to revocation or other reported consequences. This is a completed evidence-limited assessment, not a finding of no harm.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: The case shows why biometric identification and administrative enforcement need traceable evidence, notice and review paths before a disputed identification affects travel privileges.
assessment_boundaries: The use of facial recognition and its link to revocation are alleged by the affected party and not confirmed in a public agency finding.
Global Entry and TSA PreCheck are discretionary travel programmes; the record does not equate revocation with detention or loss of freedom of movement.
